We can validate Theorem 3.15 to fams with the uap under further conditions. Theorem 3.16. In Theorem 3.15, assume that B = P(X) and that Bo contains all the finite subsets of X. IfEo has the uap, then so does E. Likewise for "uniformly supported".

Proof. If all finite sets have Eo-measure zero, then the same is true for E. So assume that Eo is uniformly supported with support P. Since Bo contains all finite sets, all finite sets in P with positive measure must be singletons (by minimality). It is not hard to show that P is a support of E, so E is uniformly supported.

Similarly, we can validate the extension results when adding one set to the subalgebra. Lemma 3.17. In the context of Lemma 3.11, assume that B = P(X) and that C contains all the singletons. Then, if E has the uap, then E' can be found with the uap. As a consequence, = can be extended to a fam into K with the uap on the whole P(X). Here, "uap" can be replaced by "uniformly supported", even more, extensions of E can be found with the same support.

We ask whether (iii) → (i) of Theorem 3.8 is valid when Eo and E1 have the uap for finding = with the uap, under the condition that both Do and B1 contain all singletons. If, say, Eo is free then E1 and = must be free, but we do not know how to obtain an uniformly supported E when Eo and E1 are uniformly supported. Question 3.18. Assume that Bo and By are fields of sets over X, containing all the singletons, and Eo and E1 are uniformly supported fams with the uap on Bo and B1, respectively. Assume that Eo and E1 are compatible (in the sense of Theorem 3.8 (iii)). Is there a uniformly supported fam that extends both Eo and E1?

A strategy to solve this problem may suggest a short proof of Theorem 3.8.
